- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the following 7–14 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 7–14 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to misalign with true trend; prioritize sentiment-weighted average over pure historical trend.
